record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Is every core compact T0 space a Rudin space? A Rudin space is a T0 space in which every irreducible closed set has the Rudin property, meaning it is a minimal closed set meeting every member of some filtered family of nonempty compact saturated subsets.

evidence.quote: Question 5.15. Is every core compact T0 space a Rudin space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a $T_0$ topological space. A subset $A\subseteq X$ is called saturated if it equals the intersection of its open neighborhoods (equivalently, $A$ is an upper set with respect to the specialization order). A nonempty closed set $C\subseteq X$ is called irreducible if $C=C_1\cup C_2$ with $C_1,C_2$ closed implies $C=C_1$ or $C=C_2$.

A family $\mathcal{K}$ of nonempty compact saturated subsets of $X$ is called filtered if for any $K_1,K_2\in\mathcal{K}$ there exists $K_3\in\mathcal{K}$ with $K_3\subseteq K_1\cap K_2$. A closed set $A\subseteq X$ is said to have the Rudin property if there exists a filtered family $\mathcal{K}$ of nonempty compact saturated subsets of $X$ such that $A$ is a minimal closed set meeting every member of $\mathcal{K}$ (i.e., $A\cap K\neq\emptyset$ for every $K\in\mathcal{K}$, and no proper closed subset of $A$ has this property).

The space $X$ is called a Rudin space if every irreducible closed subset of $X$ has the Rudin property.

Recall that $X$ is called core compact if its open-set lattice $\mathcal{O}(X)$ is a continuous lattice; equivalently, for every open set $U$ and every $x\in U$ there exists an open set $V$ with $x\in V$ and $V\ll U$, where $V\ll U$ means that every open cover of $U$ has a finite subfamily covering $V$.

Question: Is every core compact $T_0$ space a Rudin space?
artifact.status_search_result: Related results in the literature show that every core compact $T_0$ space is a well-filtered determined (WD) space and that every core compact well-filtered space is sober, but the specific question of whether every core compact $T_0$ space is a Rudin space does not appear to have been resolved. No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: On T0 spaces determined by well-filtered spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every core compact T0 space is a WD space; every core compact well-filtered space is sober.
status_evidence.claim: Related properties (WD, sobriety) are established for core compact T0 spaces, but the Rudin-space question is not resolved there.

status_evidence.title: On topological Rudin's lemma, well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces Rudin spaces and WD spaces as classes between directed-closure spaces and irreducible closed sets.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the framework in which the question is posed; the Rudin-space question for core compact T0 spaces is left as a problem.
